events.title: Hong Bang Dynasty Foundation Myth
events.description: According to Vietnamese legend, the Hong Bang Dynasty established the Van Lang Kingdom, marking the mythical origin of Vietnamese history. Though lacking historical evidence, this legend holds an important place in Vietnamese culture.

events.title: Au Lac Kingdom Established
events.description: King An Duong Vuong established the Au Lac Kingdom, ruling the Red River Delta region. Au Lac is considered Vietnam's earliest state formation, developing unique bronze culture (Dong Son culture).

events.title: Han Emperor Wu Conquers Nam Viet
events.description: Han Emperor Wu conquered the Nam Viet Kingdom, establishing commanderies in northern Vietnam. Vietnam began over a millennium of Chinese rule, with Chinese culture profoundly influencing Vietnam.

events.title: Trung Sisters' Uprising
events.description: Sisters Trung Trac and Trung Nhi led Vietnamese rebellion against Han Dynasty rule, briefly establishing independent rule. Though ultimately suppressed, the Trung Sisters became Vietnamese national heroes.

events.title: Early Ly Dynasty
events.description: Ly Bon established the Early Ly Dynasty, briefly ending Chinese rule. Though the dynasty was short-lived and China soon reestablished control, it marked an important attempt at Vietnamese independence.

events.title: Battle of Bach Dang River
events.description: Ngo Quyen defeated the Southern Han army at the Bach Dang River, ending over a millennium of Chinese rule. Ngo Quyen established the Ngo Dynasty, beginning Vietnam's independence period.

events.title: Dinh Dynasty Founded
events.description: Dinh Bo Linh unified Vietnam and established the Dinh Dynasty, naming the country 'Dai Co Viet.' Dinh Bo Linh proclaimed himself 'Dai Thang Minh Emperor,' establishing an independent feudal dynasty recognized by Song China.

events.title: Ly Dynasty Founded
events.description: Ly Thai To (Ly Cong Uan) established the Ly Dynasty and moved the capital to Thang Long (present-day Hanoi). The Ly Dynasty lasted 216 years, representing a prosperous and stable period in Vietnamese history, with Buddhism strongly promoted.

events.title: Temple of Literature Built
events.description: Emperor Ly Thanh Tong built the Temple of Literature in Thang Long to honor Confucius and promote Confucian education. The temple later became the national academy, symbolizing Vietnamese education.

events.title: Tran Dynasty Founded
events.description: Tran Thu Do enthroned Tran Thai Tong, establishing the Tran Dynasty. The Tran Dynasty continued the Ly Dynasty's prosperity while facing threats from the northern Mongol Empire.

events.title: Three Mongol Invasions
events.description: Under General Tran Hung Dao's leadership, the Tran Dynasty defeated three major Mongol-Yuan invasions. The Battle of Bach Dang (1288) was the decisive victory, defending Vietnamese independence.

events.title: Ming Occupation of Vietnam
events.description: Ming Emperor Yongle exploited Ho Dynasty turmoil to occupy Vietnam, establishing Jiaozhi Province. Ming China attempted to assimilate Vietnam, triggering strong Vietnamese resistance.

events.title: Lam Son Uprising
events.description: Le Loi led the Lam Son Uprising, successfully expelling Ming forces after 10 years of struggle. Le Loi established the Later Le Dynasty, becoming a Vietnamese national hero.

events.title: Later Le Dynasty Founded
events.description: Le Loi established the Later Le Dynasty with Thang Long as capital. The Later Le Dynasty was Vietnam's longest dynasty (1428-1788), though power later declined.

events.title: Reign of Le Thanh Tong
events.description: Le Thanh Tong was one of Vietnam's greatest monarchs, implementing reforms, enacting the Hong Duc Code, conquering Champa to the south, resisting Ming China to the north, and bringing Vietnam to its peak.

events.title: North-South Division Begins
events.description: As the Later Le Dynasty declined, the Trinh and Nguyen families controlled the north and south respectively, with Vietnam effectively divided in two. The Trinh-Nguyen conflict lasted nearly 200 years.

events.title: Tay Son Rebellion
events.description: Brothers Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Lu, and Nguyen Hue launched the Tay Son Rebellion, overthrowing the Nguyen and Trinh lords. The Tay Son regime briefly unified Vietnam, with Nguyen Hue defeating Qing invasion.

events.title: Nguyen Dynasty Founded
events.description: Nguyen Phuc Anh (Emperor Gia Long) unified Vietnam and established the Nguyen Dynasty with Hue as capital. The Nguyen Dynasty was Vietnam's last feudal dynasty, lasting until 1945. The country's name became 'Vietnam.'

events.title: French Invasion of Vietnam
events.description: France invaded Vietnam under the pretext of protecting missionaries, capturing Da Nang. This marked the beginning of French colonization of Vietnam.

events.title: Treaty of Saigon
events.description: The Nguyen Dynasty was forced to sign the Treaty of Saigon with France, ceding three eastern provinces of Cochinchina and opening ports. Vietnam began falling under French colonial rule.

events.title: Treaty of Hue and French Protectorate
events.description: France forced the Nguyen Dynasty to sign the Treaty of Hue, making Vietnam a French protectorate. France established 'French Indochina,' including Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh Born
events.description: Vietnamese revolutionary leader Nguyen Ai Quoc (Ho Chi Minh) was born in Nghe An Province. He would lead Vietnam's decades-long independence struggle.

events.title: Indochinese Communist Party Founded
events.description: Under Ho Chi Minh's leadership, the Vietnamese Communist Party, Annamese Communist Party, and Indochinese Communist League merged to form the Vietnamese Communist Party (later renamed Indochinese Communist Party).

events.title: Japanese Occupation of French Indochina
events.description: During World War II, Japanese forces entered French Indochina, effectively controlling Vietnam. The Vichy French government nominally maintained rule.

events.title: Japanese Coup Against French
events.description: Japan launched the 'March 9 Coup,' overthrowing French rule in Indochina. Japan supported Emperor Bao Dai in establishing a nominally independent Vietnamese Empire.

events.title: August Revolution
events.description: After Japan's surrender, Ho Chi Minh's Viet Minh launched the August Revolution, seizing power. Emperor Bao Dai abdicated, ending Nguyen Dynasty rule.

events.title: Democratic Republic of Vietnam Founded
events.description: Ho Chi Minh read the Declaration of Independence at Ba Dinh Square in Hanoi, proclaiming the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam. September 2 became Vietnam's National Day.

events.title: First Indochina War (Franco-Vietnamese War)
events.description: France attempted to recontrol Vietnam, triggering an 8-year war. With Chinese support, the Viet Minh gradually strengthened, ultimately achieving decisive victory at Dien Bien Phu against French forces.

events.title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
events.description: Viet Minh forces under General Vo Nguyen Giap besieged the French base at Dien Bien Phu, achieving decisive victory after 56 days of intense combat. This victory ended French colonial rule in Indochina.

events.title: Geneva Conference and Vietnam Division
events.description: The Geneva Conference Agreement temporarily divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel. The North was led by Ho Chi Minh, the South by Emperor Bao Dai (later Ngo Dinh Diem). Though nationwide elections were scheduled for 1956, they never occurred.

events.title: Republic of Vietnam Founded
events.description: Ngo Dinh Diem held a referendum in South Vietnam, deposing Emperor Bao Dai and establishing the Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam), becoming president himself. The US strongly supported Diem's regime.

events.title: National Liberation Front Founded
events.description: With North Vietnamese support, the anti-government armed organization was established in South Vietnam, called 'Viet Cong' by the West. The National Liberation Front began armed struggle to overthrow Diem's regime.

events.title: Ngo Dinh Diem Coup and Assassination
events.description: South Vietnamese military launched a coup, overthrowing and assassinating the Diem brothers. Subsequently, South Vietnam's political situation remained turbulent with multiple coups.

events.title: Gulf of Tonkin Incident
events.description: The US claimed its destroyer was attacked by North Vietnamese torpedo boats in the Gulf of Tonkin (the incident's truth remains disputed). US Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, authorizing presidential military action in Vietnam.

events.title: Large-Scale US Intervention
events.description: The US began bombing North Vietnam (Operation Rolling Thunder) and deployed ground forces to South Vietnam. US military involvement rapidly escalated, peaking at 540,000 troops.

events.title: Tet Offensive
events.description: North Vietnam and Viet Cong launched massive offensives during Lunar New Year, attacking numerous South Vietnamese cities and US bases, even breaching the US Embassy in Saigon. Though a military failure, it was a major political and psychological blow to the US.

events.title: Death of Ho Chi Minh
events.description: Vietnamese revolutionary leader Ho Chi Minh died in Hanoi at age 79. His wish was to see Vietnam unified, but he did not live to witness it. After North Vietnamese capture, Saigon would later be renamed Ho Chi Minh City.

events.title: Paris Peace Accords
events.description: Vietnamese parties and the US signed the Paris Peace Accords, with US troops beginning withdrawal from Vietnam. However, fighting between North and South Vietnam continued.

events.title: Fall of Saigon and Vietnam Reunification
events.description: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon (South Vietnam's capital), and the South Vietnamese government surrendered. The Vietnam War ended, and Vietnam was reunified. This day is called 'Liberation Day' or 'Reunification Day.'

events.title: Socialist Republic of Vietnam Founded
events.description: North and South Vietnam officially unified, adopting the name 'Socialist Republic of Vietnam' with capital in Hanoi. Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City.

events.title: Cambodian War
events.description: Vietnam invaded Cambodia, overthrowing the Khmer Rouge regime and installing the Heng Samrin government. Vietnamese forces occupied Cambodia for 10 years.

events.title: Sino-Vietnamese War
events.description: China launched a war to 'punish Vietnam' (China called it 'Counterattack in Self-Defense Against Vietnam'). The war lasted about a month, with both sides claiming victory. Sino-Vietnamese relations deteriorated for a long period.

events.title: Doi Moi (Renovation)
events.description: The 6th Congress of the Vietnamese Communist Party decided to implement Doi Moi policies, transitioning from planned to market economy and expanding opening up. This was a crucial turning point in Vietnam's economic development.

events.title: Sino-Vietnamese Relations Normalized
events.description: Sino-Vietnamese relations normalized, ending 12 years of confrontation. Subsequently, economic cooperation between the two countries gradually strengthened.

events.title: US-Vietnam Normalization
events.description: The US and Vietnam established diplomatic relations, ending 20 years of hostility. The US lifted economic sanctions on Vietnam.

events.title: Joins ASEAN
events.description: Vietnam officially joined the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), marking Vietnam's integration into the regional cooperation system.

events.title: US-Vietnam Trade Agreement
events.description: Vietnam and the US signed a bilateral trade agreement, significantly reducing tariffs. This promoted Vietnamese exports and drove rapid economic growth.

events.title: WTO Accession
events.description: Vietnam officially became the 150th member of the World Trade Organization (WTO), further integrating into the global economic system.

events.title: First Elected State President
events.description: Tran Dai Quang was elected State President of Vietnam. Vietnam's political system continues under Communist Party leadership, but with continued opening in the economic sphere.

events.title: US-North Korea Summit in Hanoi
events.description: US President Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un held their second summit in Hanoi. As host, Vietnam demonstrated its rising international status.

events.title: Successful COVID-19 Response
events.description: Vietnam adopted strict prevention and control measures, successfully containing COVID-19 spread with relatively minimal economic impact. Vietnam's pandemic experience gained international attention.

events.title: US-Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
events.description: During President Biden's visit to Vietnam, bilateral relations were upgraded to 'Comprehensive Strategic Partnership,' Vietnam's highest diplomatic level. Vietnam maintains balance amid US-China competition.
